subject: pe
title: Physical Activity Project (PAP)
keyDates: Early October to mid-December 2026: Physical Activity Project window (8 to 10 weeks, about 20 to 25 hours; 2018-spec guidelines)
October 2026 and January 2027: check examinations.ie for PAP guidelines/booklet (OIDE advice)
Mid-December 2026: PAP completion date; 2027 exact date TBC by SEC circular (for comparison, 2026 cycle was 12 December 2025 completion, school upload 12-15 January 2026)
June 2027: 2.5-hour written exam (50%); the redeveloped specification is first examined in 2028
summary: The Physical Activity Project (PAP) is 20% of Leaving Cert Physical Education, marked out of 100 at Higher and Ordinary level (the same project is submitted at both; Ordinary level marks are converted from a reference scale). You choose a competitive sport and a role (performer or coach/choreographer), analyse your performance (Section A, 25 marks), set three goals with a training plan for each (Section B, 45 marks), retest and conclude (Section C, 20 marks), and are marked on overall coherence (10 marks). You submit one PDF booklet of at most 1,600 words and three short MP4 videos, one per section.

stages.name: PAP: Choose activity and role
stages.marksNote: Not marked directly, but an invalid choice puts the whole PAP at risk.

points: The activity must be a competitive sport with a national governing body affiliated to Sport Ireland, and fit the Irish Sports Council Act 1999 definition of competitive sport (organised participation aiming at improved results in competition).

Check validity three ways: the physical activity areas page of the specification, the Sport Ireland NGB finder, then the SEC (schoolsportal@examinations.ie) if still unsure. Your teacher authenticates the choice.
Affiliated but non-competitive (e.g. angling) or competitive but unaffiliated (e.g. powerlifting) are given by OIDE as invalid examples.
Do the PAP on the activity as a whole, not a single skill or exercise.
Your school makes the final decision on which activities it can support, especially outside school.
The PAP activity must be in a different physical activity area from your Performance Assessment activity. Hurling and soccer are both Games, so you could not use one for each.
Golf, triathlon or boxing may be allowed for the PAP even if not listed in the specification, but cannot be used for the Performance Assessment, which needs a specified activity.
A Studyclix teacher guide advises deciding your Performance Assessment activity first and saving your strongest sport for it, because that is where you are graded on skill.
Performer: you analyse and improve your own performance.
Coach/choreographer: you analyse and lead a peer (a senior-cycle student) through the plan. Parental consent for the peer is required.
Both roles follow the same project structure.
A PE teacher or another registered teacher on the school staff must accompany you when filming outside school, and a representative of the club must be present.
Sign the school consent forms; the club's image rules cannot be overridden by consent forms.
Keep the number of other people on camera to a minimum.

checklistCandidates: Confirm your sport has a Sport Ireland-affiliated NGB and is competitive
Pick a PAP activity from a different activity area to your Performance Assessment
Get your teacher to confirm the activity and role before you start

stages.name: PAP: Section A - needs analysis and performance analysis
stages.marksNote: Section A: 25 marks, about 700 words (2026 SEC marking scheme).

points: List what the activity demands across the areas in the guidelines: skill and technique, psychological demands, physiological demands, performance-related fitness, health-related fitness, biomechanical/movement analysis, structures and strategies, roles and relationships, diet and nutrition.
Keep a source log as you research, because you must reference everything and list sources in the bibliography.
Design a test battery from your needs analysis and run it in class under teacher supervision.
Compare every result with normative data in a table, and cite where the norms came from.
Also collect model-performer comparison, stage of learning, tactics, psychological (e.g. SCAT) and match or observation sheets where relevant.
Everyone in the class doing all the tests makes administration easier (teacher advice).
Include a brief personal introduction, your exam number, why you chose the activity, your skill level, and key findings with references.
Label every figure (Fig.1 etc.) and refer to it in the text; images must not be used to smuggle in extra text.
Interpret results; do not just describe them. The descriptors separate analytical from merely descriptive work.
Keep your data relevant to the goals you will set in Section B.
Your video must show you engaging in the activity (for example video analysis that adds to, not repeats, the written text).
Short snippets of each test (10-20 seconds) are enough; Studyclix suggests about a minute in total.
No slides of text, images or audio reflections as part of videos, and no video collages except a two-video side-by-side skill comparison (OIDE, 2025 booklet).

Excellent (22 to 25) needs a wide selection of tests or methods, relevant data presented in detail, analysis across a wide variety of factors affecting performance, and clear links to the chosen activity and to theory.

Very good (17 to 21) analyses a range of data from a variety of areas, in some detail. Good (12 to 16) covers key performance areas with some links. Below 12 means limited tools and little interpretation.
Examiners are told not to penalise skilful brevity or reward unwarranted length, so concise and accurate beats long.

checklistCandidates: Test every component relevant to your activity and compare with cited normative data
Label each figure and refer to it in the text
Interpret what the results mean for performance rather than describing them
Film short test clips that show you doing the activity

stages.name: PAP: Section B - three goals, plans, rationale and reflection
stages.marksNote: Section B: 45 marks, about 450 words. Each of three goals is marked as 4 (goal) + 7 (plan) + 2 (rationale) + 2 (reflection).

points: Set three distinct goals, each based on your Section A analysis and the demands of your activity. Two goals from the same area (agility and coordination are both performance-related fitness) do not count as distinct.
Top marks (4) need a clear, concise goal that is appropriate, measurable and time related, grounded in theory and your initial analysis.
Write each as SMART with a baseline, a target, a time frame and the test used. Example from OIDE: 20 m shuttle run from 9.4 to 10.2 shuttles over five weeks.

guide.h: Training or practice plans (3 x 7 marks)
points: Each of the three plans is marked separately. A 7 needs a clear, well developed, individualised plan in table format that applies a wide range of theoretical principles, links to your analysis and goal, and uses activities relevant to your sport.
Insert the table as an image (the scheme lists tabulated plans inserted as an image), within the 8-image limit for Section B.
Use a different approach per goal rather than three similar fitness plans.

guide.h: Rationale and reflection (3 x 2 + 3 x 2 marks)
points: The rationale (2 marks) links the plan to relevant theory and to your activity. A weak rationale scores 1.
The reflection (2 marks) is on the goal, based on actually doing the training. A reflection that says what you did and noticed scores 2.
Keep a note of each session and what you changed, so the reflection is specific.
Film real engagement in your plans, at least two samples of the same exercise at different points, to show progress.
Videos must be real time, with no images or text slides, and the three videos together must be 4 minutes at most.

checklistCandidates: Write each goal as SMART with baseline, target and deadline
Make every goal distinct and traceable to Section A data
Write one separate, followable training plan per goal
Justify each plan with principles of training
Film real, repeated engagement in the plans

stages.name: PAP: Section C - retest and concluding analysis
stages.marksNote: Section C: 20 marks, about 450 words: post-training analysis 10, reflection on the effect of training 5, next steps 5.

points: Repeat the Section A tests under the same conditions and reuse the same table so the comparison is direct.
Top marks need a thorough, relevant post-training analysis tied to your initial analysis and goals, with broad theoretical links.
State for each goal whether you achieved it, with the numbers, and why or why not.
Reflect accurately on the effects of the training and refer to performance.
Give next steps that follow from your results. A limited or missing reference to improving further scores 2 of 5.
Discuss unintended outcomes, such as changes in tests you did not target, and how you responded to challenges.
Show a short clip of each retest and engagement in the activity, adding to the text rather than repeating it.
Total of all three videos is capped at 4 minutes.

checklistCandidates: Retest everything you tested in Section A
State achieved or not for each goal with numbers and a reason
Identify unintended outcomes
Evaluate each plan and give realistic next steps

stages.name: PAP: Coherence, format limits and submission
stages.marksNote: Overall coherence: 10 marks. Breaking a restriction caps a separate presentation mark (see rules).

points: Not a separate section: the 10 marks reward a project with clear quality, communication and links to theory throughout.
Top marks need videos that add clarity and value and support the text in all three sections. Videos that support two sections score 6, one section 4.
Section B must build on A and C on A and B. Avoid repetition.
Word count 1,600 across A to C, excluding references; Arial 12; at most 28 pages; page 7 of the booklet must be completed.
Maximum 16 images in total: 4 in Section A, 8 in Section B and 4 in Section C. No image collages.

Videos: three required (one per section), at most 4 minutes in total, at most 1 GB, recorded in real time, no images, no excessive text in images or video, no video collages (a side-by-side comparison of skill and technique is allowed).
Marks are capped if you break the rules: no videos 2, one video 4, two videos 6; a non-compliant activity 2; one restriction infringement 8, two 6, three or more 4.
Schools upload four files: the PDF and the three MP4s, named to the SEC convention (for example 2026-225-A-EV-334567.mp4).
Sign P.2 to confirm the printed PDF matches the submitted version.
Proofread the printed PDF: anything not visible cannot earn marks.

checklistCandidates: Stay within 1,600 words, Arial 12
Keep the three videos under 4 minutes combined, MP4, no text slides
Link Section A, B and C
Reference every source and add a bibliography
Print and proofread the final PDF before signing P.2

criteria.name: Section A: Performance analysis
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A wide selection of tests or methods, relevant data presented in detail, analysis across a wide variety of factors, with clear links to the chosen activity and to theory.

criteria.name: Section B: Goals, plans, rationale and reflection
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Three distinct goals (4 each), three well-developed individualised plans in table format (7 each), accurate rationale (2 each) and reflection on engagement (2 each).

criteria.name: Section C: Concluding analysis
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Thorough post-training analysis linked to Section A and the goals (10), accurate reflection on the effect of training (5), appropriate next steps (5).

criteria.name: Overall coherence
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Excellent coherence, quality and clarity, with videos that support the text in all three sections.

rules: The PAP must be in a competitive sport with a Sport Ireland-affiliated national governing body.
The PAP and the Performance Assessment must be in different physical activity areas.
The PAP is your own work, done in PE class under teacher supervision; you may train with peers but submit your own report and goals.
Editing and publishing of videos is done in school under teacher monitoring.
Booklet limit of 1,600 words excluding references, Arial 12, at most 28 pages, PDF format.
Three MP4 videos (one per section), 4 minutes in total, real time, no images in video, no collages (side-by-side skill comparison allowed).
At most 16 images: 4 in Section A, 8 in Section B, 4 in Section C.
Anyone filmed has signed consent; out-of-school filming needs a teacher and a club representative present.
Filenames must follow the SEC naming convention or the Schools Portal rejects them.
You sign P.2 confirming the printed PDF matches the submission.
Missing a deadline needs an SEC-approved extension.
mistakes: Choosing a PAP activity in the same activity area as the Performance Assessment (or a non-competitive or unaffiliated sport): the mark is capped at 2.
Submitting fewer than three videos: the mark is capped at 6 with two, 4 with one and 2 with none.
Breaking a restriction (word count, image or video limits, collages, text in images): each infringement lowers the cap.
Goals from the same area (agility and coordination are both performance-related fitness).
Goals that do not come from Section A evidence.
Describing results instead of interpreting them.
Retesting only the goal-related tests in Section C.
Plan tables that are not individualised, or three similar plans for three goals.

conflicts: The 2019 NCCA guidelines describe four goals; the 2026 SEC marking scheme marks three goals and three plans (Section B is 45 marks), so use three. The scheme and the current SEC booklet decide.
Older teacher presentations give Section B as 40 and Section C as 25; the 2026 SEC marking scheme gives B 45 and C 20, which is used here.
The scheme says the video limit is 4 minutes in total and 1 GB. Check your school's SEC booklet for any change for 2027.
2027 completion and upload dates were not yet published in the sources found; the dates above are the 2026 pattern.
2018 and 2019 guidelines are older than the SEC booklets and marking scheme; where they differ, the booklet and scheme govern.
